_meta.source: prettyhtml.com, driven live in-browser via chrome-devtools MCP
_meta.technique: window.text = input; <primitive>(); read window.text — for primitive fixtures. tinymce.get('vizualisEditor').setContent(input); convertText(); read window.text — for pipeline fixtures.
_meta.legal: Black-box input/output observations only. No third-party source is reproduced here. The raw capture lives in planning/captures/ and is gitignored.
_meta.layerNote: 'layer1' is the TinyMCE round-trip alone (setContent then getContent, before any cleaner runs). 'output' is the full convertText pipeline. Our port has no layer 1, so a fixture whose work happens in layer1 must be matched by an Extras compensation, not by a layer-2 cleaner.
_meta.oursNote: 'output' is what prettyhtml.com produces. Where we deliberately differ, 'ours' records our own expected output and 'oursNote' says why. A fixture with no 'ours' must match theirs byte for byte at shipped defaults.

primitives.note: Single linear pass. The outer div is not revisited after the inner pair is deleted.
Proves cascading is a real behavior change, not a no-op. convertText calls it once.
Only the innermost pair is removed per pass.
Tag names are never compared. Deliberate divergence G — our canRemove is stricter.
Numeric form is NOT matched. Our handling both forms is an improvement, not parity.
Option 5 is entirely about non-breaking-space entities.
Option 5 does NOT touch literal whitespace runs. Ours does the opposite. Literal runs are collapsed by the unconditional pre/post-pass instead.
One space per removed tag. Ours yields 'ab' — plain-text.test.mjs currently locks in the wrong behavior.
String-pattern replace looped to idempotence, so a run of any length collapses.

pipeline.note: TinyMCE parses the curly-quoted value as unquoted, terminating at the space; 'lede”' is dropped entirely and the opening curly quote is entity-encoded into the value. Option 2 (default ON) then removes the mangled class, so their user-visible output is clean. Ours invents a bare attribute named 'lede”' that no cleaner matches, so it survives into output. Target for our fix: match this output.
A '>' inside a curly-quoted value truncates the tag and leaks the remainder into text content. Both implementations corrupt this; theirs at least yields well-formed HTML.
pipeline.oursNote: DELIBERATE (N). We accept curly quotes as attribute delimiters, so the value stays intact and the classes/IDs option removes it cleanly. Theirs truncates the tag at the '>' inside the value and leaks the remainder into text content.

pipeline.note: Layer 1 entity-encodes real smart punctuation (entity_encoding:'named'); layer 2 leaves it alone with option 9 off. Prose typography is preserved, which is why our N fix must touch attribute delimiters only.
pipeline.oursNote: DELIBERATE (layer 1). Their TinyMCE round-trip runs with entity_encoding:'named', so real smart punctuation comes back as entities. We have no round-trip and keep the literal characters, which are valid UTF-8 HTML. The opt-straighten-quotes Extra (default OFF) converts them to ASCII for anyone who wants that.

pipeline.note: ANSWERS ISSUE #22. dir="ltr" SURVIVES on prettyhtml.com — so removing it is better-than-parity, as the plan predicted. Note also that layer 1 (not any cleaner) is what strips role="presentation", aria-level, and the docs-internal-guid <b> wrapper. Our port has no layer 1, so it must handle all of that explicitly. Synthetic sample, structurally faithful to real Docs clipboard HTML; replace with a genuine paste when one is available.
pipeline.oursNote: DELIBERATE. Two default-ON Extras go past their output: opt-docs-residue strips dir="ltr" (which survives on their site), and opt-unwrap-spans drops the <span> once option 1 has emptied it of attributes. Closes issue #22.
